_status: English. Also the fallback for any key missing in another language.
_format: Flat keys, the same in every language file. Values may contain inline HTML (<a data-fp="…">, <b>, <sup>, <span data-stat="…">) and {placeholders}; keep tags, attributes and {placeholders} unchanged and translate only the text around them. data-fp links get https://fontpixel.com/<language prefix> in front. Arrays are lists of short labels. In Chinese, Japanese and Korean text write no space between CJK characters and Latin letters or digits: the page inserts a thin space itself. Keep font names, code, file formats and Unicode names (SIL OFL, BDF, locl, zh-Hant …) as they are.
meta.title: Tong Pixel Sans 通格像素黑体
meta.description: Tong Pixel Sans: a 14-pixel pan-CJK bitmap sans with its own Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and Korean forms. SIL Open Font License 1.1.
nav.label: Sections
lang.label: Language
hero.title: Tong Pixel Sans
hero.lede: A 14-pixel pan-CJK bitmap sans for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and Korean, and also for Latin-script languages, Greek, Cyrillic, Vietnamese, Thai, Arabic, Hebrew and more.
hero.note: Each character is drawn in each region’s own form: Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean. glyphs have been reviewed and approved by the author; the rest are AI-repaired and awaiting review. Try it and tell us what’s wrong.
plates.view: Four plates. Drag or use the arrow keys to change the view: left and right turn, up and down tilt.
legend.differ: Pixels that differ, coloured by region; stacked, each takes one corner
forms.title: One text, four forms
forms.p1: The four rows are the same text set in the Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and Korean faces; colour marks pixels that differ between them. The fifth row overprints all four in each pixel: top left SC, top right TC, bottom left JP, bottom right KR.
forms.p2: Drawn from the real bitmaps in the font sources.
type.title: Type something
type.p1: This is the downloadable vector font. One file holds all four regions, switched by the text’s language tag. At whole multiples of 14 px every font pixel lands on screen pixels.
shapes.title: Square and dot
shapes.p: The vector fonts come with two kinds of pixel. Square: one square per pixel, touching pixels merged into one outline. Dot: one round dot per pixel. Drag the divider to compare.
mono.title: The mono faces
mono.p: For terminals and code: half width 7 px, full width 14 px. Hanzi, kana and Hangul take exactly two columns and box drawing is half width, so tables line up.
cell.title: The cell
cell.p: Every glyph sits in a 14×14 cell. Han ink is 13×13 with one blank column on the left and one blank row at the bottom; ascent 11 px, descent 3 px. Latin letters are proportional, or 7 px wide in the mono faces.
cell.aria: A 14×14 cell with the hanzi 通 and the letters A and g
cell.k.base: Baseline: Han ink ends 2 px below it
cell.k.em: Vector: 100 units per pixel, 1,400 per em
cov.title: character sets, complete
cov.p1: glyphs. The map is Unicode’s Basic Multilingual Plane, one pixel per code point, lit where the font has a glyph. Pick a table to see where it lies; click the map to open that page of characters.
cov.p2: Not on the map: hanzi from Extension B onwards. Also included: Hebrew, Georgian, Armenian, Lao, IPA, combining marks, currency, maths, arrows, enclosed characters and many more symbols.
cov.aria: Coverage map of the Basic Multilingual Plane; arrow keys move by page, Enter opens it
why.title: Why
why.p: Looking for an open-source CJK bitmap font, to make a pixel-art game, to translate or localise an old game, or to set up a terminal or a special device? Among 12-pixel fonts there is Fusion Pixel, among 16-pixel fonts there is Unifont1: both cover a great many characters and have different Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese forms2. A similar high-quality 14-pixel font is almost impossible to find. The established fonts at this size, such as WenQuanYi Bitmap Song, efont, K14, Firefly, Shinonome Gothic and Shinonome Mincho, plus TUMBLED from 2026, and the fonts derived from them, vary widely in glyph quality, looks and component proportions, and usually cover only the common characters or forms of their target writing system. Hence Tong Pixel Sans.
why.n1: A bitmap font’s Han ink is usually 1 pixel smaller than its stated size, or 1 pixel narrower, but there are exceptions much smaller than stated, such as Galmuri and TUMBLED. So “16-pixel fonts” above means every bitmap font whose Han ink is 15x15 or 15x16, and likewise for the other sizes.
why.n2: Fusion Pixel truly separates the regional forms with locl. Unifont only offers a Japanese version with Izumi and a Traditional Chinese version by contributors, which differ somewhat in style from the original Simplified Chinese version, not only in their regional forms.
mk.title: How it is made
mk.p: This font was not drawn stroke by stroke by one person, and it is not finished. Here is how it came about:
mk.s1.p: Each region’s forms are rasterised from Source Han Sans; Latin from Source Sans 3 and Noto, hanzi from the extension blocks from Plangothic.
mk.s2.p: An AI repairs every glyph under drawing rules the author set: a component is, as far as possible, pixel-identical in every character that uses it; a character’s regional versions derive from one master and change only the strokes that are written differently. Some hanzi borrow from TsFreddie’s TUMBLED.
mk.s3.p: The author reviews, corrects and approves each glyph in an editor. Where useful, the rules behind a batch of corrections are written down and, together with the components of the newly approved hanzi, used to run step two again on some of the glyphs.
rad.h: One component, the same pixels everywhere
review.p: Left: the AI draft. Right: after the author’s review. Solid colour marks pixels added, hollow squares pixels removed.
status.p: Every distinct bitmap in the sources (aliases not counted) is one pixel below, in order of group and code point.
dl.title: Download
dl.p1: Version . Free to use, modify and redistribute under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
dl.p2: Bitmap fonts come as one file per region; each vector font holds all four regions and switches with OpenType locl by language.
dl.pcfNote: PCF only encodes 16-bit code points, so hanzi beyond the BMP are in the BDFs only. The Latin faces have no East Asian glyphs; their quotation marks and ellipsis are the narrow western ones.
dl.vectorNote: The vector fonts default to Simplified Chinese forms. Text tagged zh-Hant, zh-TW or zh-HK gets Traditional forms, ja Japanese, ko Korean; in Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text the quotation marks and ellipsis become the narrow western ones.

game.title: On a game screen
game.p: Under blue windows, scanlines and phosphor glow, 14-pixel text stays sharp. The same lines can switch between the four regions’ glyph forms.
game.hint: Press Enter, Space or click the screen to advance; arrow keys choose; Esc returns to the title.
game.screen: Game demo: Enter or Space advances, arrow keys choose, Esc returns to the title.
game.speaker: Innkeeper
game.lines: Welcome to Tong Village, hero! A night here is only 50G, with a hot bowl of noodles.
They say the Bone Tower up north hides a spellbook that reads all four scripts: Simplified, Traditional, Japanese and Korean.
Your HP is down to {hp}/48. Why not rest here this time?
game.replies: Rest well. Your HP is full! At dawn, go straight on to the Bone Tower.
Here, freshly picked herbs. You’ll need them on the road.
Take care, hero! The gate of the Bone Tower is a fearsome sight.
